At 12AM central time, I was able to catch the last bus to Wisconsin. Now that I have another 3-hour bus time, it's perfect to write something. I always hate the bus from O'Hare to Madison because it seems to take forever and corn fields are the only yet tedious scenery along the trip. For the last two months I have been moving fast in PA and SF, delivering with colleagues in different time zones, and witnessing several deals. It's a great time, and I am fortunate to spend a (short) fulfilled period of time with the most talented and indigenous colleagues at Anyscale . Thanks for everyone for reading my verbose words. Cheers for this great company and the time! 长风破浪会有时 直挂云帆济沧海

Yesterday, I wrapped up my summer as a Strategy Consulting Intern at Kearney . A few months ago I walked in not really knowing what to expect from consulting. I'm walking out with not just how to be active on Microsoft Teams and some random Excel shortcuts, but real insight into how these industries actually work. I got to work on two very different problems: an OEM & ODM market strategy for a major appliance manufacturer, and a market entry strategy in the emerging humanoid robotics space for a global tech player. Going from refrigerators to humanoids in the same summer was a pretty wild range, and a great crash course in how consulting frameworks flex across industries. A few things I'll take with me: → Structuring overwhelming problems with a MECE framework → Organizing BOM spreadsheets from the ground up → Sourcing and running expert interviews, learning to think on my feet with follow-up questions Huge thanks to my mentors, teammates, and everyone who partnered with me this summer! Now, I'm returning to Berkeley for my bachelor's. Excited to bring some of this with me into California!

I'm incredibly excited and grateful to share that I'll be joining SpaceX this fall as part of the Fall 2026 Engineering Internship/Co-op Program on the Starship Launch Fluid Systems Team at Starbase, Texas. 🚀 This is truly a dream come true for me. Since I began studying mechanical engineering, I've been drawn to designing and building aerospace hardware and seeing ideas become reality through testing and iteration. During my time at UC Berkeley, I've had the opportunity to work on liquid rocket propulsion, UAV development, and aerospace structural design. Every challenge, redesign, failed test, and lesson learned along the way has strengthened my passion for engineering and my desire to build systems that perform in the real world. Joining SpaceX has been a goal I've worked toward throughout college, and I'm incredibly grateful for the opportunity to contribute to Starship while learning from some of the best engineers in the industry. This milestone wouldn't have been possible without the support of my family, friends, professors, mentors, and teammates. Thank you for believing in me, challenging me, and helping me grow both as an engineer and as a person. A special thank you to Sophia Castellanos for coordinating the interview process and making the entire experience such a positive one. I truly appreciate all of your support throughout the process. I'm excited for what's ahead and can't wait to get started. Dreams do come true. So chase yours. 🚀 Ad Astra #SpaceX #Starship

I felt left out watching master's & PhD grads and big tech folks build cool things with parallel computing... while I didn't even own a GPU. 😅 But I needed to understand GPU hardware for my capstone computer vision projects. So I used what I had: cloud GPUs ☁️, my brain 🧠, compilers, and documentation. Docs are hard to navigate when the explanations aren't generous; so I wrote my own. 📖 16 chapters on CUDA kernels, GPU architecture, memory optimization, modern C++, and writing GPU kernels in pure Rust with CUDA-Oxide. Every concept explained from first principles, every line of code commented. For every CS engineer who wants to stay ahead and enjoy the marvelous innovation of GPU computing 🚀: 👉 https://lnkd.in/gxsXJj3S Check out the google collab notebook posted in comments for simple vector dot product and matrix multiplication code using cuda. #cuda #gpu #parallelcomputing #rust #computerscience

Last week, I spoke to a room full of LA's top security leaders on how MindFort is changing security. The consensus we’re seeing is that teams want fully autonomous red teamers testing every inch of their attack surface around the clock. This was the dream we set out to make a reality with MindFort. Giving teams the ability to test everything, everywhere, all the time. But, it is an enormous infrastructure challenge, and takes highly coordinated and scalable systems to deliver effectively. Zero human in the loop, but designed to complement and work alongside your human teams. Today, our agents can cover your entire attack surface with continuous testing 24/7. We are glad to be sponsoring OWASP events, bringing together a community of security professionals for talks and workshops.
